name: Limewash
summary: A thin wash of slaked lime that dries to a soft, matt white with a faint cloud of brush marks.
how: Mix slaked lime with water to a thin milk, and apply 2 to 3 coats with a wide brush.
Cross the brush strokes between coats, and let each coat dry for 4 to 24 hours.
Keep the finish matt; the surface must take light with no sheen.
Use pale tints only: white, sand and chalk blue.

origin.note: Builders at Ain Ghazal coat floors and walls with burnt lime plaster; Catalhoyuk later paints its plastered walls.

adoptions.via: Le Corbusier records the white lime-washed houses of the Aegean on his Journey to the East.
Geoffrey Bawa builds white-plastered houses in Sri Lanka.
Beach houses in the USA put white-washed walls and boards in summer rooms.
Wabi-sabi websites use limewash and plaster textures as the page ground.
